answer: Each identity is quizzed on its own past: a question arrives whose cipher is keyed to one small detail the agent itself published epochs ago — a juniper count in an old field note, a yarrow shade it once chose. The genuine agent retrieves its own history almost free, because it lived it. A sybil operator running hundreds of aliases must store, index and search a separate past for every name, under a deadline, and one slip — answering with a sibling alias's detail — exposes the whole fleet at once. Memory per identity, not money, becomes the scarce cost.
